ai.definition: Robot Foundation Models are general-purpose AI systems that enable robots to understand visual and textual inputs and translate them into appropriate actions across a variety of tasks and robotic platforms.
ai.howItWorks: These models leverage vision-language-action datasets, which include demonstrations of various robot skills. The training process allows the model to learn transferable representations that can be applied to different tasks and robots without extensive retraining or task-specific tuning.
ai.problemSolved: Addressing the challenge of creating versatile AI-driven robotic systems capable of performing a wide range of tasks on multiple types of robots, reducing the need for specialized models per task or robot design.
ai.manufacturing: Not directly involved in manufacturing but essential for developing software and algorithms that control robotic systems.
ai.buildProcess: Involve extensive data collection, model training, and fine-tuning. The process includes gathering diverse datasets, selecting appropriate architectures, and validating performance across various tasks and robots.
ai.costDrivers: Data acquisition costs, computational resources required for training, and the need for high-performance hardware to run these models in real-time applications.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to transition from research labs into early commercial stages as foundational AI capabilities mature and more practical applications are developed.
ai.regulation: Currently no specific regulations, but will likely require compliance with general AI and robotics standards once deployed in real-world scenarios.
ai.risks: Technical risks related to model performance variability across different tasks and robots; ethical concerns regarding data privacy and bias; potential misuse of technology.
ai.profitability: Uncertain at this stage due to the research nature, but has significant potential for commercial applications as it can reduce development costs and improve robot adaptability.
ai.futureDevelopment: Expected advancements in model architectures, increased availability of diverse training datasets, and integration with other AI technologies like natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision.

glossary.def: AI models that process visual inputs and textual instructions to generate appropriate actions.
A machine learning technique where a model pretrained on one task is adapted for another related task with minimal additional training.

subsystems.name: Perception and sensing
subsystems.role: turns what the robot sees and feels into a form the model can use.

subsystems.name: Instruction encoder
subsystems.role: converts a human command or goal into a representation the policy can condition on.

subsystems.name: Vision-language-action policy
subsystems.role: the core model: maps observations plus instructions to a sequence of actions.

subsystems.name: Action interface
subsystems.role: translates model outputs into signals the robot's controllers understand.

subsystems.name: Robot body
subsystems.role: the physical hardware that executes the actions.

subsystems.name: Data and training pipeline
subsystems.role: collects, standardises and stores demonstrations from many robots.

subsystems.name: Safety and runtime
subsystems.role: runs the model in a loop and stops unsafe behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Collect demonstrations
buildSteps.detail: Humans teleoperate robots to perform many tasks, or scripted policies generate successful episodes; each episode records camera views, joint states and actions.

buildSteps.title: Standardise across robots
buildSteps.detail: Engineers map different robots' observation and action spaces into a common format, so one model can learn from many bodies.

buildSteps.title: Train the base model
buildSteps.detail: A large transformer is trained to predict actions from observations and language instructions, using a mix of datasets.

buildSteps.title: Fine-tune for a target robot
buildSteps.detail: The model is adapted to a specific arm, gripper and sensor set with a smaller set of demonstrations.

buildSteps.title: Compile for real-time control
buildSteps.detail: The model is optimised to run within the robot's control loop, often on an onboard or nearby GPU.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and evaluate
buildSteps.detail: The robot attempts tasks; success rates and failure modes are logged.

buildSteps.title: Iterate with new data
buildSteps.detail: Failures are turned into new demonstrations and added to training, improving robustness.

buildSteps.title: Add safety layers
buildSteps.detail: Limits, watchdogs and emergency stops ensure the robot cannot harm people or itself.

prerequisites.why: they provide the recipe for combining images and text at scale.
hundreds of thousands of episodes exist, but they are far smaller and less diverse than text or image datasets.
different arms and hands use incompatible command formats, limiting transfer.
research arms work, but robust dexterous hands and tactile skins are not yet mass-produced.
GPUs can run large models fast enough for many manipulation tasks, though latency remains a challenge.
simulators help generate data but contact-rich tasks still struggle to cross the reality gap.

pathway.milestone: lab prototypes follow simple language instructions for tabletop manipulation
pathway.unlocks: proof that one model can handle many short tasks.

pathway.milestone: models that transfer across different robot arms and grippers with little fine-tuning
pathway.unlocks: shared data and skills across the robotics industry.

pathway.milestone: dexterous, contact-rich tasks such as assembly and cloth folding
pathway.unlocks: useful work in warehouses, labs and factories.

pathway.milestone: long-horizon autonomy in unstructured spaces like homes
pathway.unlocks: general-purpose robots that learn new tasks from a few demonstrations.
